title: Pat Novak, for Hire
paragraphs: A dark, sharply written San Francisco detective series starring Jack Webb as waterfront operator Pat Novak, whose jobs repeatedly lead into murder, corruption, and clashes with Inspector Hellman.

San Francisco hard-boiled detective drama centered on waterfront operator Pat Novak. The frozen 26 objects represent 24 surviving historical programs plus two alternate-transfer objects. Regional OTRR collector numbering is preserved alongside Haendiges national-run numbering and RG network/AFRS record numbers.

GRH documents the program through Represented 1946 Jack Webb regional survivors (October 13, 1946 to November 24, 1946) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], Represented 1947 Ben Morris regional survivors (August 3, 1947 to November 30, 1947) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]], and 1949 national ABC run (February 13, 1949 to June 25, 1949) on [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]].

Among the most extensively documented contributors in the GRH holdings are [[person|jack-webb|Jack Webb]] (performer on 22 recordings), William P. Rousseau (producer on 21 recordings, director on 20 recordings, and performer on 1 recording), Basil Adlam (composer on 20 recordings, conductor on 20 recordings, and music on 1 recording), George Fenneman (announcer on 20 recordings), Tudor Owen (performer on 10 recordings), [[person|raymond-burr|Raymond Burr]] (performer on 9 recordings and announcer on 1 recording), and Jack Lewis (performer on 5 recordings).

The program is also connected in the archive to [[org|org.0d7b5c86680811cc|ABC Radio Network]] (broadcast on network), [[org|org.a3129b8eb67efa37|KECA]] (originated at station), [[org|org.4798d1172deaae2c|Armed Forces Radio Service]] (rebroadcast by), [[org|org.0207d811941f7fb5|KGO]] (originated at station), and [[org|org.0207d811941f7fb5|KGO]] (aircheck from station).

Its indexed subjects and listening characteristics include San Francisco waterfront and dockside life, hard-boiled private investigation, murder and violent crime, deception, aliases and hidden identity, blackmail, corruption and coercion, and money, gambling and criminal schemes.

GRH also places the series in documented historical contexts including KGO regional hard-boiled detective production, Jack Webb / Ben Morris / Jack Webb lead transition, 1949 national ABC run, and Collector numbering and alternate transfers.

Programs with especially strong personnel connections in the GRH knowledge graph include [[show|escape|Escape]] (14 shared credited people), [[show|richard-diamond-private-detective|Richard Diamond, Private Detective]] (14 shared credited people), [[show|lux-radio-theatre|Lux Radio Theatre]] (13 shared credited people), [[show|the-whistler|The Whistler]] (12 shared credited people), and [[show|yours-truly-johnny-dollar|Yours Truly, Johnny Dollar]] (12 shared credited people).
